questions.question: What is formed when several systems function together?
questions.fact: Several systems functioning together form an organism.
questions.explanation: Several systems functioning together form an organism.

questions.question: Why can people usually not see individual cells with the naked eye?
questions.fact: Individual cells are too small to be seen with the naked eye (with few exceptions).
questions.explanation: Individual cells are too small to be seen with the naked eye.

questions.question: What are the two broad categories that all cell types are grouped into?
questions.fact: All cell types are grouped into two broad categories: prokaryotic and eukaryotic.
questions.explanation: All cell types are grouped into prokaryotic and eukaryotic categories.

questions.question: What do scientists use to study cells?
questions.fact: Scientists use microscopes to study cells.
questions.explanation: Scientists use microscopes to study cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a tissue?
questions.fact: Examples of tissues are muscle tissue, connective tissue, and nervous tissue.
questions.explanation: Muscle tissue is an example of a tissue.

questions.question: How does a right-side up specimen facing right look through a microscope?
questions.fact: A specimen that is right-side up and facing right on the slide appears upside-down and facing left when viewed through a microscope, and vice versa.
questions.explanation: The fact states it appears upside-down and facing left when viewed through a microscope.

questions.question: What combines to form an organ?
questions.fact: Several tissues combine to form an organ.
questions.explanation: The fact states that several tissues combine to form an organ.

questions.question: What happens if a slide is moved left while looking through a microscope?
questions.fact: If the slide is moved left while looking through the microscope, it appears to move right; if moved down, it appears to move up.
questions.explanation: Moving the slide left makes it appear to move right when viewed through the microscope.

questions.question: How are animal, plant, fungal, and protist cells classified?
questions.fact: Animal, plant, fungal, and protist cells are classified as eukaryotic.
questions.explanation: The fact states that these cells are classified as eukaryotic.

questions.question: What is the diameter of the head of a pin?
options: About two hundredths of a meter (mm)
About two thousandths of a meter (mm)
About two millionths of a meter (mm)
About two tenths of a meter (mm)
questions.answer: About two thousandths of a meter (mm)
questions.fact: The head of a pin is about two thousandths of a meter (mm) in diameter.
questions.explanation: The fact states the head of a pin is about two thousandths of a meter (mm) in diameter.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of an organ system?
questions.fact: Examples of organ systems are the digestive system, circulatory system, or nervous system.
questions.explanation: The fact states that the digestive system is an example of an organ system.

questions.question: What are most cell images taken with a microscope called?
questions.fact: Most images of cells taken with a microscope are called micrographs.
questions.explanation: Most cell images taken with a microscope are called micrographs.

questions.question: What do several cells of one kind form when they interconnect and work together?
questions.fact: In multicellular organisms, several cells of one particular kind interconnect and perform shared functions to form tissues.
questions.explanation: Cells of one kind interconnect and perform shared functions to form tissues.

questions.question: What is the diameter of a typical human red blood cell?
options: About eight millionths of a meter (8 µm)
questions.answer: About eight millionths of a meter (8 µm)
questions.fact: A typical human red blood cell is about eight millionths of a meter (8 µm) in diameter.
questions.explanation: A typical human red blood cell is about eight millionths of a meter (8 µm) in diameter.

questions.question: What is the smallest unit of a living thing?
questions.fact: A cell is the smallest unit of a living thing.
questions.explanation: The fact states that a cell is the smallest unit of a living thing.
